learn.title: Capacity Factor Explained
learn.intro: Capacity factor reveals how much energy a plant actually produces versus its maximum potential. Understanding this gap helps optimize grid investments and renewable integration.
learn.c1_text: Capacity factor = (actual output / max potential) × 100. A 100 MW coal plant running 8,760 hours/year has 100% CF. Solar at 25% CF produces ~2,190 GWh/year.
learn.c2_text: Solar's 25% CF vs. nuclear's 90% CF shows why overbuilding renewables or adding storage balances grid needs without fossil fuels.
learn.c3_text: India's solar CF averages 15-20% due to monsoon variability. Policy pushes hybrid plants (solar + wind) to boost aggregate CF to 25%+.

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels
learn.intro: Bifacial panels capture light on both sides, boosting efficiency. This innovation is critical for maximizing solar yields in diverse environments.
learn.c1_text: Standard panels absorb light front-side only. Bifacial panels use transparent backsheets to capture reflected light, gaining 10-30% more energy.
learn.c2_text: In desert installations, albedo from sand boosts bifacial gains to 25%. A 100 MW bifacial farm in Rajasthan generates 120 GWh/year vs. 90 GWh for monofacial.
learn.c3_text: India's bifacial module shipments grew 40% in 2023. MNRE mandates bifacial panels for all new utility-scale solar projects above 50 MW.
learn.stat2: 15% efficiency gain in bifacial vs. monofacial

learn.title: India ISTS Waiver Policy
learn.intro: India's ISTS waiver policy slashes transmission costs for renewable projects, accelerating clean energy deployment.
learn.c1_text: Developers pay reduced ISTS charges (10-15% of project cost) instead of full rates, lowering upfront investment barriers.
learn.c2_text: A 100 MW solar project saves ₹20-30 crore in transmission fees. This enables competitive pricing at ₹2.50/kWh vs. ₹3.00/kWh without waivers.
learn.c3_text: Since 2019, ISTS waivers helped add 45 GW of solar/wind. Rajasthan's Bhadla Solar Park benefits from 100% ISTS waiver eligibility.

learn.title: Grid Balancing Basics
learn.intro: Real-time grid balancing ensures electricity supply matches demand. This is vital for integrating variable renewables like solar and wind.
learn.c1_text: Grid operators adjust supply (via generators) and demand (via load shedding) every 2-5 seconds to maintain 50 Hz frequency in India.
learn.c2_text: Solar's 25% CF and wind's intermittency require 30-50% flexible resources (gas peakers, storage) to maintain stability.
learn.c3_text: India's grid loses ₹40,000 crore/year from imbalances. PM-Surya scheme mandates 10% DER integration by 2025 to test balancing solutions.

learn.title: Green Steel Production
learn.intro: Hydrogen replaces coal in steelmaking, cutting CO2 emissions by 70%. This technology is key for decarbonizing heavy industry.
learn.c1_text: Hydrogen reduces iron ore to liquid iron at 2,000°C, replacing 1.5 tons of coal per ton of steel. Sweden's HYBRIT plant produces 10,000 tons/day.
learn.c2_text: Hydrogen reacts with carbon: 3H2 + CO2 → 2H2O + C. This carbon acts as a reducing agent, avoiding 2 tons of CO2 per ton of steel.
learn.c3_text: India's steel sector emits 300 MT CO2/year. MNRE targets 10% green steel by 2030, requiring 15 GW of green hydrogen electrolyzers.

learn.title: Renewable Purchase Obligation
learn.intro: RPO mandates DISCOMs to source X% of power from renewables, driving clean energy adoption and reducing fossil fuel dependence.
learn.c1_text: India's RPO targets: 50% renewables by 2030. DISCOMs must procure 25% from solar/wind by 2025, with annual increases of 2-3%.
learn.c2_text: Non-compliant DISCOMs pay ₹3-5/kWh penalties. Gujarat's 2023 RPO shortfall cost 12 DISCOMs ₹1,200 crore in fines.
learn.c3_text: RPO compliance drove 80% of India's 150 GW renewable additions (2014-2024). Tamil Nadu's 20% RPO led to ₹4,500 crore in renewable investments.
